messages.subject: Compile PyStan on MSVC13(x64) for Python3
parts:
Hello everybody,

I am totally new to Stan and PyStan. I would like to use this library after many good comments that I have found online, but I am in troubles since I have issues in the compilation of Win7 x64 and Python3 using MSVC13(x64) as compiler.

I followed these directions to add the compiler flags: http://pystan.readthedocs.org/en/latest/windows.html

Then, I faced this known issue with Boost 1.54: http://stackoverflow.com/questions/19740377/how-can-i-compile-boost-with-vs2013-64-bit
that I roughly fixed simply substituting the 'boost' folder with the same folder present in Boost 1.55. Surprisingly, it seems to work. Any comment on this?

Now I am getting another type of error:

error C3861: 'assert_not_arg': identifier not found

Before moving forward in this Pandora's box, is somebody on the list being able to compiler PyStan with a similar configuration? I'd like to avoid Python distributions as Anaconda.

Any help is very welcome!!

I may have done some progress.

First, I attempted to compile 2.4.0 but I got the same type of errors.

Looking around I have found that this type of error was quite common when MS started to include their <stdint.h>

In brief, I got a successful compilation of 2.5.0.1 with this 3 simple steps:
1. substitution of folder with Boost_1.54.00 with Boost_1.55.0
2. addition of /EHsc (not /Ehsc as reported here: http://pystan.readthedocs.org/en/readthedocs/windows.html) to 'extensions_extra_compile_args'
3. modification at 'stack_alloc.hpp', row 8 to read: #if _MSC_VER < 1600

parts:
Hi John,

It seems that you are attempting to build with Python 2.7 rather than Python 3.4.. as you can read everywhere in your building report.

About the error, did you check if you actually have this file?
pystan/stan/src/stan/gm/grammars/term_grammar_inst.cpp: No such file or directory

However, if you want to follow these instructions( https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/stan-users/Uu7y-Zg_MF8 )
you have to use PyStan 2.4.0. My post is about using the last version of PyStan and not using Anaconda.

messages.subject: Boost versions
parts:
[changed subject]

Stan is currently on Boost 1.54, because of restrictions
on size imposed by CRAN (the R repository); 5MB is too
large for them. We're not on CRAN yet, but Ben and Jiqiang
are working on it.

Boost finally got 1.57 out, so we're now several versions
behind.

We may wind up upgrading the Boost libs in everything but
RStan in the next release.

I don't know about PyStan, but in both RStan and CmdStan,
you can specify your own Boost lib paths. I don't think
anyone's tested beyond 1.54, though, so you'd be on your
own with that.

- Bob

(Nota bene: building PyStan *from source* on Windows is currently unsupported.)

Hi Shota,

We did make a patch to Stan so it would support VS2008
(https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/pull/633) and I think we'd be open to any
additional patches that are required. Currently neither Stan nor PyStan requires
C++11 support. In short, I think VS2010 should work if VS2008 works. That said,
there could have been a breaking change in 2.5.0.

We'd love to have someone who has experience with compiling Python extensions on
Windows as part of the PyStan team. Right now the collective extent of our
knowledge is really just this : https://pystan.readthedocs.org/en/latest/windows.html

Thanks,

Allen
